title: Too Hot to March! D.C. Cancels July 4th Parade
summary: Imagine getting ready to march in a huge parade, then hearing it's canceled because it's just too hot outside. That's what happened to 80 students from a Nebraska marching band who traveled all the way to Washington, D.C., for the big July 4th parade. The parade was supposed to celebrate America's 250th birthday, but extreme heat made it unsafe. The National Weather Service warned that the heat index—a measure of how hot it really feels when you combine temperature and humidity—could hit 115°F. That's dangerously hot! Organizers said keeping everyone safe was the top priority. The heat already broke records. On Friday, it hit 102°F at Reagan National Airport, the hottest July 3rd since 1966. Saturday could be the hottest July 4th ever in D.C. Other cities had to cancel events too. Philadelphia, where the Declaration of Independence was signed, called off a parade and moved fireworks to midnight. In New Jersey, a parade was canceled because of "oppressive heat and humidity." Around 120 million Americans are facing extreme heat this weekend. But the fireworks show on the National Mall is still happening tonight at 10:30 p.m., with a speech from President Trump. Just watch out—there might be thunderstorms with strong winds too!
why_it_matters: Extreme heat can cancel fun events and reminds us that listening to weather warnings is key to staying safe, especially when temperatures feel like 115°F.

background_read: The United States celebrates Independence Day on July 4th every year to mark the adoption of the Declaration of Independence, the historic document that declared the country's freedom from Britain in 1776.

Washington, D.C., where the nation's biggest celebrations take place, often experiences hot and humid summers. The National Weather Service (a U.S. government agency that provides weather forecasts and warnings) warned that the heat index—a measure combining temperature and humidity—could reach 115°F, making it dangerous to be outside.
At Reagan National Airport (one of the airports serving Washington, D.C.), the temperature hit a record 102°F on July 3rd, the hottest July 3rd since 1966.
Article_Structure: WHO: A marching band of 80 students from Nebraska, parade organizers, the National Weather Service, and President Trump (giving a speech at the fireworks).
WHAT: The Washington, D.C., July 4th parade was canceled because of extreme heat, but the fireworks on the National Mall are still happening.
WHERE: Washington, D.C., with similar cancellations in Philadelphia (where the Declaration of Independence was signed) and New Jersey.
WHY: The heat index—a measure of how hot it feels combining temperature and humidity—was forecast to reach 115°F, making it unsafe for marching. Organizers made safety the top priority.

perspectives.description: They put safety first. With a heat index of 115°F, marching could cause heatstroke, so canceling the parade was the right call.
They are disappointed after traveling all that way and practicing for nothing. The cancellation ruined a big moment they had looked forward to.
